paragraph: Single-family is the market in Ridgefield Park, with 30 sales over six months at a median of $617,500, mostly three-bedroom colonials with two full baths and a handful of capes mixed in. Two-thirds sold above list and the sale-to-list ratio is 1.02, but the median days on market is 30, so call this competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes are moving, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. Sales ran from $375,000 up to $980,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Two-families are the tightest part of town, six sales at a median of $857,500 with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.08 and a median of 13.5 days on market. That is investor and multi-generational demand meeting almost no supply. Condos and townhouses barely register at three sales and a median of $475,000, and co-ops came in at four sales with a median of $162,750 and 64 days on market. Co-ops carry board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction, which not every buyer is aware of going in. On the monthly numbers, February through June ran three or four closings each, too thin to read a trend, and July's 12 closings fit the normal early-summer volume peak. If you're weighing tiers, the question is whether you want the space of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, or the lower price point of a co-op.
